Q: Understanding read() function from unistd A:

I want to take care of how to get user letter from CLI

Your program is not reading from "CLI" but a terminal.
So the behavior of read() is determined by the configuration of the terminal, that is, its termios settings, which is reported by the stty command.

I would also like to receive some instructions on how to understand read() function deeply.

So besides studying the man page for read(), the man page for termios is also relevant (as well as how your terminal is configured, e.g. for canonical or raw mode).

Q: Offsetting Anchor Links with Fixed Header A:

There's a problem with old answers, because in this day and age the solution is, of course,

h2 { scroll-margin-top: 90px; } or, preferred

h2 {scroll-margin-top: var(--masthead-depth); } because this is a very useful number in all sorts of contexts.

Q: How do you use operator=()? A:

The problem is that the assignment operator you've provided for derived has a non-const lvalue reference parameter of type int& which can't bind to rvalues like 5.

But since you've also provided a converting ctor derived::derived(int), the argument 5 can be implicitly converted to an object of type derived using this converting ctor(hence the name). To avoid this, you can make this converting ctor explicit which will disable the implict conversion of 5 to a temporary derived object. When to make constructor explicit in C++ lists some scenarios like yours, where explicit can/should be used.

How can I fix this

Change the parameter of the assignment operator such that it can bind to rvalues. So, you can either change it to take const int& or int.

Also see When to make assignment operator virtual.
